check_1_gcc_semantics_and_macro.gcc_behaviour_measured: GAP9 GCC 7.1.1 (-march=rv32imcxgap9) treats float16/float16alt as PREDECLARED FILE-SCOPE TYPEDEF NAMES, not keywords. Accepted by GCC: block-scope 'int float16 = 3;', a parameter named float16, a struct member named float16, 'struct float16 {..}' (tag namespace), a label named float16, a local 'typedef int float16;' that shadows it, 'typedef float16 float16;' (only a -Wpedantic warning), sizeof, casts, _Generic(x, float16: ..). Rejected by GCC: file-scope 'int float16;', a function or enumerator named float16/float16alt ('redeclared as different kind of symbol, previous declaration ... cc1'), 'typedef short float16;' (conflicting types). GCC 7 has no _Float16 on this target ('_Float16 is not supported on this target'), so 'typedef _Float16 float16;' only appears in clang-specific code. GCC predeclares the names even with plain -march=rv32imc. In C++ g++ accepts them but mangles f(float16) as '_Z1f' (broken, no parameter type), so there is no C++ ABI to match whatever the mechanism.
where_the_macro_diverges_from_gcc: Block-scope identifiers (variables, parameters, labels, local shadowing typedefs): GCC accepts, clang errors.
Struct/union members and struct/union/enum TAGS named float16/float16alt: GCC accepts, clang errors.

'typedef float16 float16;' (a compatible redefinition): GCC accepts, clang sees 'typedef _Float16 _Float16' and errors. 'typedef _Float16 float16;' in clang-only code (the gap9-sweep shim) errors too.
'#ifdef float16' / 'defined(float16)' is true in clang and false in GCC. '#undef float16' removes the type in clang only.
Stringizing or pasting through a macro layer that expands its argument: XS(float16) gives "_Float16", CAT(t,_add) via T(float16) gives '_Float16_add'. GCC gives "float16" / 'float16_add'.
Diagnostics and -E output name _Float16/__bf16 instead of float16/float16alt (cosmetic).

Gating differs on purpose: GCC has the names for every -march; clang only when xpulpf16alt/xpulpfvec (+zhinx for float16) are on (xgap9). Checked with -dM for rv32imc, rv32imc_zfinx_zhinx, rv32imc_xpulpv2, rv32imc_zfinx_zhinx_xpulpv2, rv32imafc_zfh, rv64gc_zfh: no macro. xgap9: both. zfinx_xpulpf16alt: float16alt only. zfinx_zhinx_xpulpv2_xpulpfvec: float16 only.

The cases GCC also rejects (file-scope variable/function/enumerator named float16, 'typedef <other type> float16;', e.g. Emulation/Gap.h:16-23 under __EMUL__/__FLOAT_EMUL__ and audio-framework fft_int.h:89) are errors with the macro too, so they behave the same.

check_2_HasFullBFloat16.what_it_changes: In clang 20 HasFullBFloat16 is read in two places. hasBFloat16Type() is already true on RISC-V (RISCV.h:116), so nothing changes there. QualType::UseExcessPrecision (clang/lib/AST/Type.cpp:1625) returns false for BFloat16, so __bf16 arithmetic, including compound assignment, is no longer promoted to float and rounded once per expression. Each operator is emitted as fadd/fmul bfloat and rounded after every operation. It changes neither usual arithmetic conversions nor promotion rules (__bf16 op float is still float; mixed _Float16/__bf16 still goes through half, which is T7/Q3). It also leaves ABI, calling convention, mangling (DF16b comes from e62175736551 for __bf16 in any case), sizeof/alignment and predefined macros unchanged: a C and C++ -dM diff against int-20 shows only the two new macros. One more effect: -Xclang -fbfloat16-excess-precision=standard can no longer bring excess precision back under xpulpf16alt (numeq column cl-bf16-oldexcess = cl-bf16), as on X86/ARM.
check_2_HasFullBFloat16.gating: Only xpulpf16alt. Verified: __bf16 (a+b)*c at -O2 emits 0 fpext/fptrunc and 2 bfloat ops with rv32imc_xgap9, and 4 fpext/fptrunc and 0 bfloat ops with rv32imc_zfinx_zhinx_xpulpv2 and rv32imc_zfinx_zhinx. With rv32imc_zfinx_xpulpv2 the IR is byte-identical to int-20's, apart from the clang version string.

check_2_HasFullBFloat16.linking: GAP9 libgcc (rv32imcxgap9/ilp32) exports only __extendohfdf2/__truncdfohf2 for bfloat, and no __truncsfbf2. This is not a new dependency: without HasFullBFloat16, any __bf16 result already needed __truncsfbf2 (the int-20 clang emits 1 call for (a+b)*c and 1 for a plain float->__bf16 conversion). The change raises the count per expression (2 for (a+b)*c). No SDK file that linked before stops linking because of this commit: every SDK float16alt file failed to compile before. The newly compiling float16alt files (e.g. DctLibraryf16a.c, PreProcessingf16a.c) need compiler-rt's truncsfbf2.o, or GAP9 libgcc plus T3, to link. That is the design's known T3 dependency (design table row T4: 'T3, without it __bf16 needs __truncsfbf2'), and the result file discloses it.
